drivingQuestion: What does the mishna add by ruling that one does not sell a surplus tool in order to buy a tool of the scarce type?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is left standing here; it is answered in the next unit by מהו דתימא ... קא משמע לן.

segments.he: הָיָה לוֹ מִין אֶחָד. פְּשִׁיטָא! כִּי הֵיכִי דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ עַד הַשְׁתָּא, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי סַגִּי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The mishna teaches that if «one had» many tools of «one type» that he was allowed to keep and few tools of one other type, e.g., three adzes and one saw, the treasurer does not sell tools of the type of which there are many in order to purchase for him tools of the type of which he has few. The Gemara asks: Isn’t it «obvious? Just as» it was «sufficient for him until now» to work with one saw, «now too» a single saw should be «sufficient for him.»
